newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran says oil income 6 pct below budget forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Iran says oil income 6 pct below budget forecasts.

text.p: Iran's earnings from oil exports in the three months to June 21 reached $4.1 billion, some six percent below the budgeted amount, Iranian Oil Minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh said on Wednesday.

Aghazadeh, quoted by state-run Tehran radio, said the $4.1 billion exports of crude oil and petroleum products were "higher in comparison with the same period last year" but stood at 94 percent of the amount forecast in the budget for the Iranian year which started on March 21.
He did not give comparative figures for last year.

Aghazadeh said Iran's crude oil sold in the period for an average $17.10 per barrel, 40 U.S. cents lower than the budgeted level, but he expressed hope that the price would rise with increasing demand in the coming months, the radio said.
Oil is Iran's largest single earner, contributing some 40 percent of the state budget revenue.
Iran produces 3.6 million barrels per day (bpd) of crude. Its exports of 2.5 million bpd make it the world's third largest exporter after Saudi Arabia and Norway. FS
